turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know why my son's grade was changed to a zero before anyone called me.
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
Okay. "Last three essays." What did they show, specifically? And how does a reread this morning explain a zero entered before anyone called me?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. That's an impression, and I don't deal in those. What did you find in those essays that puts a zero in the gradebook?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here, Hale? A thoughtful kid doesn't get a zero without a conversation first. I'm still waiting on what you actually have.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
Caring isn't a procedure, Hale. If you don't want a fight, take the zero off. Then we can talk about whatever you think you have.
